evidence: Ch313 project boundary (sources/appsupp1_p4.png, Figure 2) georeferenced this pass: scale bar measured at 107 px = 0.4 mi (166.2 px/km); anchor point = boundary's SW corner (pixel ~952,912), matched to the closest point on OSM US-287 way 21326169 to the site longitude, (33.9771, -98.7949), 0.88 km from that way's nearest vertex. Under a north-up affine transform, the boundary's blue outline (detected by color threshold, pixel bbox x:491-1206, y:136-912 excluding the legend) spans lat 33.977-34.019, lon -98.825 to -98.778.

The land-disturbance area found via the human-reviewer tip is at lat 34.0475, lon -98.7712 -- 3.1 km north of the boundary's northernmost edge (34.019) and slightly east of its NE corner (-98.778). It falls OUTSIDE the Short Creek Solar / Wichita Solar I Ch313 boundary.

The disturbance itself is real (not a false read): imagery/s2_cornercandidate_2022-07-15.png (2022-07-15) shows natural brush/pasture with dark plow-row texture at that location; imagery/s2_cornercandidate_2026-07-15.png (2026-07-15) shows a cleared, notched-boundary graded area with interior dirt tracks, small bright structures, and a small dark pond -- see zoom imagery/s2_cornercandidate_2022vs2026_zoom.png. Cause is unconfirmed from 10 m imagery alone (could be an oil-lease pad/tank battery -- Wichita County is oil country and similar small dot features appear throughout the search grid -- or another unrelated development); it is NOT attributable to 24INR0201.
Negative-sweep confirmation: the SW block (site centroid 33.985,-98.795, imagery/key/s2_swblock_2022-07-15.png vs s2_swblock_2026-07-15.png) remains unchanged bare farmland through 2026-07.

Negative-sweep of the rest of the human-flagged xwide top-right region and grid: imagery/search/pA-pD_2026-07-15.png and the original corner-candidate chips imagery/s2_corner_2022-07-15.png / s2_corner_2026-07-15.png (34.02-34.05 lat, -98.775 to -98.81 lon, 3 km buffer) show only ordinary contour-plowed farmland, oil-lease pads/tanks, and creek/pond features -- no construction signature within the actual (georeferenced) project boundary anywhere in the swept grid.

10 m Sentinel-2 resolution cannot rule out survey stakes or minor road work within the true boundary, but any real solar-scale grading (racking pads, substation pad, roads to a ~600-800 MW plant) would be visible and is NOT present within the georeferenced boundary limits.

cod_assessment.drift_risk_note: CORRECTED 2026-07-18: unchanged from the original assessment. An initial re-read of this pass had lowered drift_risk to 'medium' based on apparent early site-prep, but rigorous georeferencing of the Ch313 boundary map showed that disturbance is ~3.1 km OUTSIDE the project boundary and not attributable to Short Creek Solar (see construction.evidence). No construction evidence within the actual project boundary was found, so the original 'high' drift-risk reasoning stands.
reasoning_evidence: The reported queue COD (2027-12-17) is INCONSISTENT with the currently-executed contractual COD. The First Amended and Restated IA between AEP Texas and Wichita Solar I, LLC, signed 2026-04-14 (PUCT 35077-2471), sets the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date for Generation Phase 1 (Solar, 24INR0201) at '44 months from the execution date of the Original Agreement' = 44 months from 2024-10-02 = approximately 2028-06-02. The original IA (2024-10-02, 35077-1963) had a Scheduled COD of 50 months = ~2028-12-02; the amendment pulled that in by 6 months while adding a co-located storage phase (27INR0029) with its own COD 56 months out = ~2030-06. The queue-report 2027-12-17 pre-dates BOTH by roughly six months to a year — the queue COD lags the actual contract.

Independent imagery evidence, now including a rigorously georeferenced check of the full Ch313 boundary (not just the site centroid), shows the site is completely undeveloped as of 2026-07-15 within the actual project boundary (lat 33.977-34.019, lon -98.825/-98.778). To reach commercial operation on a ~625-830 MW solar-plus-storage plant by Dec 2027, the developer would need to have already completed civil grading, be well into racking, and have the substation transformer pad ready — none of which is visible within the boundary. Reaching Dec 2027 COD from a bare-land starting point in ~17 months is not physically credible for a project of this scale.

Reaching the contractual 2028-06 COD is credible given typical build cadence on flat Texas ranchland: mobilization 2027-Q1, grading through 2027-Q4, racking + modules 2028-Q1-Q2, commissioning into In-Service 2028-04 / COD 2028-06.

Risk: amended IA already pulled Solar COD in by 6 months (from 2028-12 to 2028-06) while adding storage & BTM scope — this is aggressive; one further slip on either the interconnection facilities side (AEP Poisson buildout) or the equipment side (Sungrow inverter delivery) would push COD to late 2028 or Q1 2029. Amended IA rule that any 12+ month extension triggers a paid-for re-study caps single-step drift but doesn't rule out serial 6-month adjustments.

For: $20M security posted and retained through the amendment; TotalEnergies parent (investment-grade, real 4 GW US pipeline via Core Solar acquisition Jan 2023); Ch313 with Electra ISD executed and 3 years of compliance reports; amendment ADDS scope (co-located battery + BTM load) — developers don't do that on paper projects.

Net: the project is REAL and financially serious, but the queue-report COD of 2027-12-17 is optimistic by roughly 6 months relative to the signed contract, and the absence of any visible construction within the georeferenced project boundary 17 months before that date effectively rules it out. Independent estimate = 2028-Q3 (contractual COD 2028-06-02 plus a small buffer for typical solar commissioning slippage, given one 6-month schedule change is already in the history).

correction_pass.reason: Human reviewer flagged apparent solar-site/large-construction imagery in the top-right corner of imagery/s2_2026-07-15_xwide.png (~lat 34.05, lon -98.78). The original no_activity verdict had only ever imaged a 2 km buffer around the site point (33.985,-98.795) and never looked at that corner, ~7.3 km away.
correction_pass.outcome: Investigated thoroughly and ruled OUT. Real, new land disturbance was found at lat 34.0475, lon -98.7712 between 2022-07 and 2026-07 (genuine change, not a misread) -- but a rigorous pixel-to-geo transform of the Ch313 boundary map (sources/appsupp1_p4.png), anchored on an OSM-matched point on US-287 and scaled via the map's own printed scale bar, shows the project boundary's true northern edge is at lat ~34.019 -- 3.1 km SOUTH of the disturbed area. The disturbance is real but lies OUTSIDE the Short Creek Solar project boundary and is not attributable to 24INR0201 (likely oil-lease or other unrelated ranch development, common in this county). Verdict remains no_activity for 24INR0201; drift_risk remains high.
correction_pass.process_note: An intermediate draft of this pass incorrectly concluded 'early_construction' by shape-matching the disturbed area to what looked like a second lobe of the Ch313 boundary, without georeferencing the map numerically. A subsequent advisor review flagged that shape-matching alone was weak evidence and that the map could be georeferenced exactly using its scale bar plus known road/landmark coordinates; doing so reversed the conclusion. Final verdict (no_activity, boundary confirmed by rigorous georeferencing) is the one recorded here.
